title: Sex differences in pacing during half-marathon and marathon race
authors: Cuk I, Nikolaidis PT, Knechtle B
population: 17,525 finishers of the 2017 Vienna City Marathon (4,807 men and 1,278 women) and half marathon (7,624 men and 3,816 women), five race segments
findings: Absolute average change of speed across five race segments was 5.46% (men) and 4.12% (women) in the marathon.
It was 3.60% (men) and 3.36% (women) in the half marathon: pacing was more even in the half marathon in both sexes.
The sex difference in pacing was smaller in the half marathon than in the marathon.
limitations: One race, one year; city-marathon field; no finishing-time strata in the abstract; average change of speed is a summary of variability, not a measure of second-half slowing.
implications: Half-marathon pacing is more even than marathon pacing in a mass-participation field; speed varies about 3.4 to 3.6% across segments in the half against 4.1 to 5.5% in the marathon. Supports keeping a first-half pacing line to the marathon and not extending it to the half.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (Res Sports Med 28:111-120; online 2019-03-21, volume year 2020). Abstract read on Europe PMC. Crossref lists no correction, erratum or retraction notice (checked 2026-11-16).
